title: Comparing Vision–Language Models in Psychological Drawing Analysis
content: Children’s drawings serve as rich clinical and developmental assessment tools, yet their interpretation remains subjective. The emergence of vision–language models (VLMs) offers a novel, automated approach to this challenge, raising a critical question: do different AI models derive the same clinical narrative when presented with the identical drawing? To investigate this, we evaluated five VLMs—GPT-4 Vision, Claude Vision, Gemini, Grok, and LLaMA—interpreting 315 children’s drawings under a shared, projective-inspired framework. We systematically compared the models’ outputs across emotional tone, thematic focus, linguistic style, and semantic similarity. Our findings reveal a fundamental split between perception and expression: while the systems converged strongly on basic semantic content and topic structure—agreeing on what they see—they diverged significantly in sentiment, clinical vocabulary, tone register, and interpretive stance. This divergence yields a distinct, identifiable “interpretive fingerprint” for each model. We conclude that model choice fundamentally shapes the interpretive narrative in ways that matter for applied use. Given their stylistic divergences and unique interpretive biases, VLMs cannot serve as objective, standalone evaluators, but should instead be utilized strictly as supplementary instruments under professional clinical supervision.
